name: Virgental & Umbalfälle
kurzbeschreibung: The Virgental in Nationalpark Hohe Tauern is a paradise for mountaineers and nature lovers, featuring the famous Umbalfälle.
preis: Kostenlos (Parkplatz Ströden ca. 7 € pro Tag; Kutschfahrt ca. 8–10 €)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Virgental unfolds as one of East Tyrol's most unspoiled and dramatic high-alpine sanctuary valleys, nestled peacefully between Matrei, Virgen, and Prägraten am Großvenediger. Flanked by the glacier-crowned 3,000-meter peaks of the Venediger and Lasörling mountain ranges, this sun-drenched valley delights nature enthusiasts with preserved farming hamlets, lush pastures, and torrential alpine torrents. The undisputed crown jewel at the valley terminus is the celebrated Umbal Waterfalls (Umbalfälle): here, the nascent Isel River—Central Europe's last remaining free-flowing glacier river—crashes down towering glacial rock escarpments in thundering cascades and turquoise whirlpools. Created as the first water educational trail in Europe, the gorge path offers intimate perspectives on the raw hydrological might born of the Umbalkees ice sheet. Untamed by modern ski development, the Virgental represents an enduring haven for hikers, families, and wilderness purists.

Route & Requirements

Visiting the Umbal Waterfalls is one of the premier family excursions in Hohe Tauern National Park. Starting from the Ströden hiking trailhead, an easy, gently graded gravel carriage road traces the rushing river for roughly 40 minutes to reach the historic Pebellalm and Islitzeralm chalets (1,513 m; easy grade T1, accessible for rugged all-terrain strollers). Just beyond the pastures, the official waterfall loop commences: well-secured stone trails and cantilevered steel observation balconies suspend walkers directly above roaring spray and glacial plunge pools (approx. 1 hour round-trip loop, 150 vertical meters gain, moderate grade T1/T2). Seasoned trekkers can extend onward into the secluded upper valley to historic Clarahütte (2,038 m) or tackle multi-day traverses on the Lasörling and Venediger high-altitude trails (grade T2/T3). Sturdy hiking shoes with reliable tread and a light water-resistant windbreaker are advisable against moisture. Leashed dogs are permitted throughout the national park.

Visit & Arrival

By public transport, travelers take ÖBB mainline trains to Lienz railway station and connect to regional Postbus 951, running via Matrei straight to Prägraten and the Ströden trailhead during peak summer. Motorists navigate via Felbertauern highway B108 to Matrei, following valley road L24 westward through Virgen to the large parking grounds at Ströden (parking fees apply; EV charging and park info pavilion on-site). During summer, horse-drawn carriages also ferry visitors from Ströden up to Islitzeralm.

Tips

Walk out onto the dramatic overhang viewing platform suspended over the central cataract to inhale the micro-dispersed alpine water mist—renowned for its refreshing and respiratory wellness benefits. Afterward, relax on the sun deck of Islitzeralm enjoying authentic handmade East Tyrolean "Schlipfkrapfen" dumplings topped with sizzling browned butter.
saison: Mai bis Oktober (Wasserschaupfad im Winter schneebedeckt)
